 I think I was duped when they told me I’d someday have to flee to the wilderness to escape Sabbath persecution! 
 Features 
 aunt sevvy 
 2 November 2026  | ​​ 
 Dear Aunt Sevvy, 
 I think I was duped in my youth, when they told me that someday I would need to flee to a remote cave to hide from people who want to persecute me for keeping the Sabbath. Seriously, Aunty: what good would that do nowadays, given GPS and all the technologies that connect us? Could I actually hide? 
 Gentle Reader: 
 We live in a world where anonymity has become impossible. Even Doug Batchelor couldn’t remain undiscovered in his cave anymore.  
 The Millerites were treated badly by their original churches. Uriah Smith and Ellen White employed obscure prophecies in Revelation to build that rejection into paranoia about persecution by Roman Catholics and other Protestants. Some Adventists have sold everything and moved to isolated country places. Pathfinder children are taught to “live off the land.” All to prepare for an imagined persecution!  
 Was the expectation of persecution ever true, or has it simply been a useful narrative? Because in the past almost 200 years, never have we been hunted for being Sabbath keepers. Never have we had to flee to the wilderness. There have been the occasional Sabbath work or school conflicts, sometimes addressed in court. But in most places in the world we’re safe and part of society.  
 Let’s remember that Jesus himself says he has no idea when he’ll return. The only “sign” of his return Jesus offers is actually seeing him! 
 A recent Adventist Today magazine was themed, “In Search of a Gracious Eschatology,” and Aunty urges you to read it. The continued drumbeat of urgency and persecution is unhealthy, and it should end.  
 Aunt Sevvy
